title: The hanifs
hook: a few people refused the idols and sought the religion of Ibrahim

segments.voice: Yesterday, the House among the idols. Your line was: the house remembered. What old thing did you pass, and what was it first made for? Day seven hundred two.

A man stands with his back pressed against the wall of the Ka'ba, facing the crowd instead of the idols. Asma, the daughter of Abu Bakr, remembered him there, and Sahih al-Bukhari keeps her memory. He is calling out to the people of Quraysh: none of you follows the religion of Ibrahim except me. His name is Zayd ibn Amr. He has no book of his own and no community behind him. Just a wall at his back and a refusal. Today's word is what people called someone like him.
screen: `A MAN, HIS BACK TO THE KA'BA.` → `NONE OF YOU BUT ME.` → `ZAYD IBN AMR.`

segments.voice: The word is hanif. Pickthall renders it upright; others explain it as one who turns from false worship toward the one God. The Qur'an uses it more than once for Ibrahim. In surah three, Pickthall translates: "So follow the religion of Abraham, the upright. He was not of the idolaters." In surah sixteen, Ibrahim is "by nature upright." Hanif is the word under both. So in a Mecca crowded with idols, tradition remembers a few people who looked at all of it and said no. They had no scripture and no congregation. They had a name, Ibrahim, and a conviction that the House belonged to one God. Zayd ibn Amr is one of them remembered by name in al-Bukhari, and the reports about him are concrete. He would not eat meat sacrificed to idols. His reason, as al-Bukhari gives it: God created the sheep, sent down the rain, and grew the grass, and still people slaughtered it in names other than His. Asma remembers, too, that when a father meant to kill his little daughter, Zayd would step in. Don't kill her, he would say. I'll feed her for you. And another report says he traveled north asking learned people about true religion, was pointed back to the religion of Ibrahim, and lifted his hands and declared that he was on it. The sirah says he died before the revelation began. So a hanif wasn't a member of a movement with a meeting place. Some readers describe the word as a direction rather than a club: someone already turned toward God, before there was a road to walk on.
screen: `HANIF: TURNED TOWARD THE ONE GOD.` · `THE RELIGION OF ABRAHAM, THE UPRIGHT.` · `NO MEAT FOR IDOLS. DON'T KILL HER.` · `A DIRECTION, NOT A CLUB.` · then, large: `BY NATURE UPRIGHT.`

segments.voice: The practice: hold one quiet conviction. Sit tall, and let your breath settle. Find one thing you hold to quietly, even when the room around you doesn't: that people deserve dignity, that a promise is a promise, that God is one, whatever is truly yours. Don't argue for it. Just hold it, the way Zayd leaned his back against that wall: steady, not loud. Breathe around it. If you pray, you can ask Allah to keep you firm on it. If you don't, simply notice what it's like to stand on something. The bell holds the time.
Hanif. Upright: one who turns from false worship toward the one God. The Qur'an's word for Ibrahim. Today's word.
Your line: a few kept looking. Today, keep your conviction in one small act that nobody will notice. Tomorrow, Zamzam found again. Day seven hundred two.

howItsDone: The Qur'an calls its listeners to follow the religion of Ibrahim, the upright (3:95), and its verses calling Ibrahim hanif are recited in classes and sermons on pure worship of the one God.

fork.setup: you're Zayd ibn Amr in a Mecca full of idols. you've turned away from them, but you have no scripture and no community. what do you do?
options: give up and rejoin the crowd.
travel, asking learned people about the religion of Ibrahim.
carve a new god of your own.
fork.reveal: a report says he traveled north asking, was pointed back to the religion of Ibrahim, and declared he was on it.

trapdoor: what you thought: an old word for a pious person.
what it means: one who turned from the idols toward the one God of Ibrahim, before there was a community to join.
what a scholar hears: the Qur'an applies it to Ibrahim (3:95, 16:120), and al-Bukhari remembers Zayd ibn Amr as one such seeker.

notes: Pickthall wording of 3:95 and 16:120 quoted from memory; please confirm.
Bukhari numbers 3826–3828 cited from memory; confirm.
In Bukhari 3827 Zayd meets a Jewish and a Christian scholar who each point him to the religion of Ibrahim; the script says only 'learned people' to avoid making either a foil. Confirm this is fair.
'The sirah says he died before the revelation began' rests on Ibn Ishaq; confirm.
Hanif glossed from a root about turning or inclining (h-n-f); confirm against a standard lexicon.
Other hanifs named by Ibn Ishaq (e.g., Waraqa ibn Nawfal) are left for later days.
